chains.title: CTCF gain at nearby dELS alters PYDC2 expression

links.claim: Hypothesis: CTCF binds the alt G allele more strongly than the ref T. No QBiC-SELEX model or data for CTCF is supplied, and E04/E09 report no CTCF ChIP-seq peak over this variant in HCT116; the binding-direction claim is therefore unsupported and speculative.
The variant lies 42 bp from dELS EH38E2269392 and does not overlap a cCRE (E03), but there is no evidence that this dELS is active in HCT116 or that the variant changes its activity.

PYDC2 is the nearest protein-coding gene, 19.5 kb upstream (E02), and the variant is intronic in PYDC2-AS1 (E01); however, GTEx reports no significant eQTL for this variant, including in colon transverse (E07,E10), so the gene link is only distance/annotation-based.
HCT116 is the supplied expression context, but E04 reports no HCT116 TF ChIP-seq peak at this base, and there is no positive evidence that a CTCF-PYDC2 axis is active in HCT116.

A CTCF-gain-to-PYDC2-to-colorectal-cancer effect is speculative; GWAS, Open Targets, and eQTL evidence are null (E05-E07,E10), and the literature hits do not directly link this variant or PYDC2 to colorectal cancer (E08).

checks.why: This directly tests whether CTCF occupies the variant in the relevant cell line. A positive HCT116 peak would make H1 binding less missing; absence would further collapse H1.
A colon cis-eQTL for PYDC2 or nearby genes would directly strengthen the gene link, while another null result would keep the distance-only gene link weak. It also informs H2.gene and H3.gene.
If PYDC2 is not a dependency in colorectal cancer models, the PYDC2-to-colorectal-cancer phenotype link remains unsupported. This also informs the shared phenotype logic in H2.
